questions.question: What was the primary objective of the campaign launched by the Government of India in October 2014?
questions.explanation: The passage states that the SBM was initiated on 2 October 2014 to eliminate open defecation and improve solid waste management.
questions.source_sentence: Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM), Swachh Bharat Abhiyan or Clean India Mission is a country-wide campaign initiated by the Government of India on 2 October 2014 to eliminate open defecation and improve solid waste management and to create Open Defecation Free (ODF) villages.

options.A: To launch the first formal sanitation programme in rural India
options.B: To replace the Total Sanitation Campaign with a new municipal policy
options.C: To construct 90 million toilets specifically for menstrual health awareness
options.D: To eradicate open defecation and enhance the management of solid waste

questions.question: How does the passage characterize the relationship between the Swachh Bharat Mission and the Total Sanitation Campaign?
questions.explanation: The passage clarifies that SBM is a restructured version of the Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan, which was launched in 1999 as the Total Sanitation Campaign.
questions.source_sentence: It is a restructured version of the Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan which was launched by the Government of India in 1999, as Total Sanitation Campaign.

options.A: The Swachh Bharat Mission is a restructured evolution of the earlier Total Sanitation Campaign
options.B: The Total Sanitation Campaign was a pilot project created by the Swachh Bharat Mission
options.C: The Swachh Bharat Mission was replaced by the Total Sanitation Campaign in 1999
options.D: Both programs were launched simultaneously to address different sanitation needs

questions.question: What is the intended purpose of the current phase of the Swachh Bharat Mission?
questions.explanation: The passage explains that Phase 2 is being implemented to reinforce the achievements of Phase 1.
questions.source_sentence: Phase 1 of the Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) lasted until 2 October 2019, and Phase 2 is being implemented between 2020–21 and 2024–25 to reinforce the achievements of Phase 1.

options.A: To initiate the construction of the first 90 million toilets in India
options.B: To replace the scientific waste management goals of the first phase
options.C: To strengthen the outcomes achieved during the first phase of the mission
options.D: To launch the Total Sanitation Campaign as a new national initiative

variables.PASSAGE:
Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM), Swachh Bharat Abhiyan or Clean India Mission is a country-wide campaign initiated by the Government of India on 2 October 2014 to eliminate open defecation and improve solid waste management and to create Open Defecation Free (ODF) villages. The mission also emphasizes scientific solid waste management, including segregation, collection, processing, and disposal of municipal waste. The program also aims to increase awareness of menstrual health management. It is a restructured version of the Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan which was launched by the Government of India in 1999, as Total Sanitation Campaign.
A formal sanitation programme was first launched in  India in 1954, followed by the Central Rural Sanitation Programme in 1986, the Total Sanitation Campaign (TSC) in 1999 and the Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan in 2012. These earlier programs laid the foundation for integrated sanitation and waste management approaches, which were further expanded under the Swachh Bharat Mission. Phase 1 of the Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) lasted until 2 October 2019, and Phase 2 is being implemented between 2020–21 and 2024–25 to reinforce the achievements of Phase 1.
Initiated by the Government of India, the mission aimed to achieve an "open-defecation free" (ODF) India by 2 October 2019, the 150th anniversary of the birth of Mahatma Gandhi through construction of toilets. According to government data, approximately 90 million toilets were constructed during this period.
